question: The Forest Department changed its strategy, making a beginning in the Arabari forest range of Midnapore district, at the insistence of a far-seeing forest officer named:
solution:
The correct answer is __**AK Banerjee**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The Forest Department changed its strategy in the Arabari forest range of Midnapore district at the insistence of a far-seeing forest officer named** A.K. Banerjee**.
 
• Banerjee recognized the unsustainable practices of traditional forestry, which often involved clear-cutting and neglecting the needs of local communities. He believed that involving local people in forest management would lead to better conservation outcomes.
 
• In **1972**, Banerjee initiated a participatory forestry program in the Arabari range, where local villagers were given rights to forest resources in exchange for their involvement in protection and management. This innovative approach, known as the Arabari experiment, has been widely recognized as a successful model for community-based forest management in India.
